- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often undercorrects; increase forecast slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; lag 1–2 periods in adjusting for sentiment-driven moves.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 70, apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
